hypothesis: Generate complete detailed-route columns from shared geometric resource prices, then select compatible columns collectively, avoiding repeated independent ordering/ripup searches.
mechanism: A full-graph shortest-path oracle generates new complete paths using nonnegative primitive and shared-junction resource prices. Exhausted restricted selection discovers every exact incompatible primitive/junction row across accumulated column pairs, once per pair. Projected subgradient updates price violated capacities. An exact integral restricted master chooses one compatible column for every original pair task. The column pool is generated online rather than fixed before routing.
proof_limit: The master is exact only for the generated finite columns. Price updates are a bounded subgradient policy, not an exact restricted-master LP dual solve, branch-cut-price method or optimality certificate. Missing columns, finite-graph exhaustion, incomplete master exploration and work/round limits remain unknown for the board and never become upstream exclusions.
domain: Ordinary unscaled Pipeline9 nodes with two to twelve explicit pair tasks, finite valid coordinates, and endpoints inside the prototype's nominal rectangle and available layers. The graph contains endpoint-aligned/uniform wires, split endpoint chords and interior through-via sites. Finite domains outside this family are rejected explicitly before graph construction. Original portfolio candidates and their expansion/effort caps remain unchanged.
resources_and_identity: Task indices retain exact pair/endpoints independently of electrical root aliases. Wire order, layer and requested width are represented by complete route witnesses and actual copper primitives. Through vias occupy the full stack. Same-root copper sharing does not exempt owner-independent drill spacing: exact shared sites may be reused, while distinct sites use the caller's actual via hole diameter and hole-edge clearance. Route regionId preserves native node assignment through force improvement and repair.
physical_validation: Every accepted witness passes fixed-obstacle and real-board/pad/copper DRC. Conversion uses the actual caller hole diameter and minimum hole gap. All distinct output drill pairs, including sites within a single task, are checked before acceptance. A rejected within-task drill or final DRC witness rejects only this candidate and creates no learned constraint or infeasibility claim.
budgets: The new candidate has 40000 times pair count times effort engine steps and a fixed 64 pricing-round limit. Pricing expansions, exact master states and all-pool resource discovery consume that work budget. Existing candidates retain their original budgets and expansion clock. The master stops at a compatible integral selection; it does not claim globally minimum wirelength.
setup_costs: Candidate constructors prepare immutable task/obstacle ownership context when the ordinary high-density portfolio is instantiated. Shared graph allocation occurs only on the candidate's first executed step. Both occur inside ordinary high-density execution and must be included, including costs of losing candidates. End-to-end paired Blacksmith elapsed is primary; counters or oracle-only timing are not CPU savings.
positive_validation: Two forced initial conflicting columns cause a proved capacity row, price update, genuinely new full-graph detours and a compatible integral selection
64 randomized finite restricted-pool cases match exhaustive integral assignment feasibility and preserve path costs/endpoints
Ordinary P9 test proves genuinely new priced columns activate on the default path
Physical layer-transition, full-span barrel, fixed rotated-obstacle, foreign-pad and real-board checks
Same-net legal separate drills and exact shared-drill reuse, actual caller rule propagation and within-task drill rejection
Exact legitimate overhang eligibility and regionId preservation
Async routes/counters and unchanged native portfolio budget regressions
controlled_negative: The physical two-trace symmetric crossing in a 6mm square with two layers, 0.15mm traces, 0.3mm vias and 0.1mm clearance has available via solutions, yet this price policy exhausts its unchanged 64-round cap. Exact edge/junction prices can chase equivalent planar crossings instead of pricing the global obstruction. This remains an explicit unknown-policy regression; budgets were not increased to manufacture a success.
telemetry: Phase stats distinguish oracle calls and expanded vertices, genuinely new versus duplicate columns, master attempts/states/compatible successes, processed column-pool pairs, resource and junction rows, violated capacities, price updates, geometry checks, pool/master widths, final validation/rejection and all budget exits.
falsifiers: Default activation generates few useful new columns or has low physical acceptance
Equivalent conflicts migrate between resources without producing needed topologies or via choices
Column/pool compatibility or setup costs exceed removed native routing work
Any strict endpoint, width, copper, board or drill regression remains
Paired full-board speedup is far below the proposed breakthrough scale despite meaningful activation
performance_claim: None before audited paired Blacksmith results. The controlled failure limits this subgradient policy/resource model; it does not disprove route-column architectures with stronger obstruction rows or solved LP relaxations.
